claims: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft and its four-astronaut crew are in space.
The Artemis II mission had a successful liftoff at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Artemis II mission is executing a 10-day journey.
The Artemis II mission is moving away from the upper stage of the SLS rocket.
The Artemis II mission is beginning its trajectory toward the Moon.
As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission's location is in transit to the Moon.
As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission is departing low-Earth orbit.
Solar array wings (SAWs) have successfully deployed.
Solar array wings (SAWs) are generating power for the Orion capsule named Integrity.
The crew is performing a 10-day test flight to test systems for future moon landings.
The goal of the Artemis II mission is to circumnavigate the Moon.
The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed mission to circumnavigate the Moon in over 50 years
